stories.headline: Amit Shah speaks to Andhra CM, promises aid over Cyclone Murasu
stories.title: Amit Shah speaks to Andhra CM, promises aid over Cyclone Murasu
stories.summary: Amaravati, Nov 3 : Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke to Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu over the phone about the impact of Cyclone ‘Murasu’ which crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast early Tuesday. HM Shah assured him of every possible assistance from the Centre. The Union Home Minister said in a post on ‘X’ that NDRF and SDRF teams are already on the ground, helping those affected. He stated that the Government of India stands with the people with an unwavering resolve. The Home Minister inquired about the impact of Cyclone ‘Murasu’. “I assured him that the Central Government will provide all kinds of assistance and support. Already, NDRF and SDRF teams are on the ground, undertaking relief measures and standing as a support for the people in the cyclone-affected areas. The Government of India stands with the people of Andhra Pradesh with a firm resolve to face any kind of situation,” he said. Earlier, Chandrababu Naidu briefed Amit Shah on the situation following Cyclone ‘Arnab’ and the subsequent arrival of Cyclone ‘Murasu’. The Chief Minister explained the crop losses and damage to property reported in various districts. He thanked the Union Minister for sending a central team to assess the damage caused by cyclone ‘Arnab’. The Chief Minister sought adequate assistance from the Centre to help the state recover from the impact of the successive cyclones. Meanwhile, CM Naidu has thanked Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and the people of Karnataka for standing with Andhra Pradesh during Cyclone Murasu. The Andhra Pradesh CM posted on ‘X’ that their timely support in our hour of need will never be forgotten." CM Shivakumar had earlier posted about the help being extended to Andhra Pradesh. “Our teams are on their way to Andhra Pradesh to support relief and restoration efforts in the cyclone-affected areas. Karnataka stands with the people of Andhra Pradesh, and we will extend every possible support during this difficult time,” the Karnataka Chief Minister said. Shivakumar had posted earlier that he spoke to Chandrababu Naidu and assured him of Karnataka’s full support as Andhra Pradesh grapples with the devastation caused by Cyclone Arnab. “With over 15,000 electricity poles uprooted by Arnab, the restoration of power infrastructure is critical, and Andhra Pradesh has sought Karnataka’s assistance in this effort. Our Energy Department is coordinating the assistance, with Energy Minister Shri K.J. George closely monitoring the situation.” He revealed that Karnataka is deploying 500 skilled men, along with the necessary equipment, to expedite restoration works and facilitate the early restoration of electricity supply in the cyclone-affected areas. --IANS

stories.headline: J&K Consumer Commission Holds Bajaj Allianz Liable For Unjustified Deduction From Flood Insurance Claim
stories.title: J&K Consumer Commission Holds Bajaj Allianz Liable For Unjustified Deduction From Flood Insurance Claim
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Jammu and Kashmir State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Srinagar, comprising President (Officiating) Nighat Sultana and Member Maheep Gupta, has held Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd.
liable for deficiency in service after it deducted a portion of an insurance claim despite the surveyor assessing the flood-related losses at a higher amount.

The Commission found that the insurer failed to produce documentary evidence supporting the deductions or establishing the complainant's consent to a negotiated settlement and directed it to pay the differential claim amount along with compensation for delay and litigation costs.
The complainant, Showkat Ahmad Mir, a resident of Batapora, Khanabal, Anantnag, filed a consumer complaint against Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd.
and Jammu and Kashmir Bank Ltd., alleging deficiency in service over the settlement of an insurance claim arising from flood damage to his insured business unit.
The complainant stated that his business unit suffered losses due to floods during the currency of the insurance policy.
The loss was assessed by the insurance company's surveyor, Tahir Ahmad Shah, at ₹44,56,374 through an assessment report dated June 16, 2015.
The insurance company subsequently settled the claim in May 2017 by paying ₹36.90 lakh to the complainant.

Aggrieved by the deduction of ₹7,66,374 from the surveyor-assessed loss, the complainant approached the Jammu and Kashmir State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Srinagar, seeking payment of the deducted amount, along with interest at 12.40%, compensation of ₹1.50 lakh for unfair trade practices and ₹50,000 towards litigation expenses.
The insurance company contended that the complainant had been asked to submit sale and purchase bills, VAT returns and other supporting documents but had opted for a negotiated settlement instead.
It claimed that he had agreed to accept ₹37 lakh as full and final settlement and submitted a discharge voucher.
After deducting a reinstatement premium of ₹10,000, the company paid ₹36.90 lakh through a cheque dated May 22, 2017.

stories.headline: India, Israel vote against UNGA draft on regional conventional arms control
stories.title: India, Israel vote against UNGA draft on regional conventional arms control
stories.summary: United Nations, Nov 03: India and Israel have voted against a draft resolution in the UN by Pakistan and Belarus on conventional arms control at regional and subregional levels, with New Delhi saying countries' security concerns are not confined within regional boundaries. The draft resolution, titled ‘General and complete disarmament: Conventional arms control at the regional and subregional levels’, was approved by the UN General Assembly’s First Committee on Monday with 180 votes in favour, two against and no abstentions. India and Israel were the only countries to vote against the resolution in the 193-member UN body. Explaining India's vote, First Secretary at India’s Permanent Mission to the UN, Anmol Sher Bedi said conventional arms control was a global issue. “We are not fully convinced that it should be pursued primarily in regional and sub-regional contexts,” Bedi said while delivering India’s Explanation of Vote in the UNGA First Committee. He said New Delhi voted against the resolution consistent with its past position. India also questioned the resolution's request to the UN Disarmament Commission to consider formulating principles that could serve as a framework for regional agreements on conventional arms control. “We read this request with a certain degree of curiosity,” Bedi said. He pointed out that the Commission had already adopted by consensus guidelines and recommendations on regional disarmament in 1993, guidelines on conventional arms control and disarmament in 1999, and recommendations on practical confidence-building measures in the field of conventional weapons in 2017. “That makes three consensus outcomes on this very subject in the very body now being asked to start from scratch,” he said. “We fail to understand why a subject already deliberated at length needs another round of deliberation unless the aim is to keep the UN disarmament machinery busy,” Bedi added. Bedi also objected to the resolution's approach towards maintaining a balance in defence capabilities within a region or subregion. “This assumes that the security concerns of States politely stop at their regional borders. They do not,” he said. “Those concerns, as everyone understands for well-known reasons, extend beyond narrowly-defined regions and subregions. More importantly, the notion of preserving balance in a region or a subregion appears unrealistic,” Bedi said. The resolution notes that conventional arms control needs to be pursued primarily in regional and subregional contexts since most threats to peace and security in the post-Cold War era arise mainly among states located in the same region or subregion. It also expresses the desire to promote agreements aimed at strengthening regional peace and security “at the lowest possible level of armaments and military forces.” India separately voted against a paragraph that referred to conventional arms control proposals made in the context of South Asia. The paragraph noted with “particular interest” initiatives in different regions, including consultations among some Latin American countries and “the proposals for conventional arms control made in the context of South Asia”, while recognising the relevance of conventional arms control to regional security. The resolution also states that “militarily significant States and States with larger military capabilities have a special responsibility” in promoting agreements for regional security.

stories.headline: Indian national from Tamil Nadu dies in Nepal helicopter crash
stories.title: Indian national from Tamil Nadu dies in Nepal helicopter crash
stories.summary: Kathmandu, Nov 3 : The foreign national killed in a helicopter collision in Nepal on Tuesday has been identified as an Indian, officials said. One person was killed and another injured when two helicopters collided in the mountainous Solukhumbu district of eastern Nepal on Tuesday morning. Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Nabin Raja Budhathoki, chief of the District Police Office in Solukhumbu, told IANS that Vasanth Kumar, an Indian national from Tamil Nadu, was killed in the accident. "The injured person is a New Zealand national of Indian origin," he said. Both were passengers aboard a Fishtail Air helicopter that collided with an Air Dynasty helicopter as the two helicopters attempted to land at a helipad in the Pheriche area of Solukhumbu district on Tuesday morning, according to preliminary reports. Budhathoki said the pilot of the Fishtail Air helicopter also sustained minor injuries. However, the Air Dynasty helicopter had no passengers on board, Nepali authorities said. The Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal said in a press release that an AS350 helicopter operated by Air Dynasty Heli Service Pvt. Ltd., registration number 9NAOD, had departed from Lukla Airport for Pheriche. The other helicopter, an AS350 operated by Fishtail Air Pvt. Ltd., registration number 9NAJR, had departed from the Gorakshep area for Pheriche carrying two foreign nationals. The two helicopters collided while landing at Pheriche at 8:12 a.m. local time, the authority said. Videos circulating on social media appear to show the rotor blades of the two helicopters colliding as the aircraft approached each other, before they fell to the ground. Local media reports said the injured passenger had been brought to Kathmandu for further treatment. "We are preparing to send the body of the passenger killed in the accident to Kathmandu for a post-mortem examination," Budhathoki said. The Everest region is a major tourist destination, and helicopters operate frequently in the area, transporting foreign tourists and supporting rescue operations. --IANS

stories.headline: Uttarakhand avalanche leaves eight trekkers missing, search ops on
stories.title: Uttarakhand avalanche leaves eight trekkers missing, search ops on
stories.summary: Kolkata, Nov 3 : Eight members of an expedition team, including five from West Bengal’s Bankura district, have gone missing after being caught in an avalanche and a sudden snowstorm while trekking in Uttarakhand, a government official said on Tuesday. The missing trekkers from Bankura have been identified as Tapas Bauri, Ratan Ghosh, Rintu Mandal, Uday Ghosh and Manoj Khawas. The first four are residents of Salbani village, while Manoj belongs to Keshra village in the same district. Of the other three missing members, two are from Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarkashi in Uttarakhand. The five trekkers from Bankura had left for Uttarakhand on October 24 and were scheduled to return home in early November. Following the incident, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari expressed concern over the safety of the missing trekkers and said the state government was coordinating with the Uttarakhand authorities. "Deeply concerned about the five young trekkers from Bankura: Rintu Mondal, Uday Ghosh, Ratan Ghosh, Tapas Bauri and Manoj Khawas, who have gone missing during the Kedartal trek in Uttarakhand following severe weather and heavy snowfall," Adhikari wrote in a post on X. He said his government was in constant touch with the Uttarakhand government and its State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) to monitor the situation. "Through our Resident Commissioner’s Office in New Delhi and State Disaster Management channels, we are actively seeking regular updates on the extensive search and rescue operations currently underway to locate and rescue our boys," he said. The Chief Minister said the Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) and the Superintendent of Police of Bankura district had been assigned the responsibility of maintaining round-the-clock coordination with the Uttarakhand SDRF, local district authorities and administrative officials at the site. He added that the state administration had contacted the distressed families in Bankura and was extending all possible logistical and emotional support. "We stand firmly with the families, and no effort is being spared to ensure the safe and swift return of our youths. We pray for their safety and well-being," Adhikari added. According to information available, a 12-member expedition team, comprising four Sherpas and an assistant, had set out from Gangotri for Kedartal. The team began its trek from the base camp on the scheduled day. However, while negotiating the mountainous terrain at an altitude of around 4,000 metres, most of its members were caught in a sudden snowstorm and went missing. Four members of the expedition, including a Sherpa and the assistant, eventually managed to reach their destination on October 30. They subsequently informed the authorities that the remaining eight members of the team were missing. Following the report, the Uttarakhand government launched a search and rescue operation. A team of the Uttarakhand SDRF, assisted by a helicopter operated by the Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority, has been searching the mountainous region for the missing trekkers over the past two days. However, there has been no breakthrough so far. The Uttarakhand government said adverse weather conditions in the high-altitude region were intermittently hampering the rescue operation. The local administration has also contacted the families of the missing trekkers and assured them of all possible assistance. Bankura District Magistrate Anish Dasgupta said on Tuesday that the district administration had contacted the families after receiving information about the incident and assured them of all possible help. Family members said they had been in regular contact with the trekkers after their arrival in the mountains. However, there had been no communication with them for the past two to three days. The mobile phones of the missing trekkers were also switched off, adding to the anxiety of their families. --IANS

stories.title: Ram Madhav accuses Congress of attempting ‘regime change’ through anarchy
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 3: BJP national vice president Ram Madhav on Tuesday accused the Congress of attempting to fulfill its avowed objective of “regime change” through “anarchy, violence and riots as it could not win power through democratic means of electoral battle.” “But people are with Modiji and this became evident again during their opposition’s much hyped Ramlila Maidan rally, where 23 parties together could hardly bring 50,000 or 60,000 people against their haughty claims of 1 million people. BJP, even in a normal rally in an assembly constituency of Jammu, can bring 5000 people. This explains that the people want whom,” he maintained. Madhav, accompanied by J&K BJP general secretaries Gopal Mahajan, Baldev Singh Billawaria, chief spokesperson Sunil Sethi and other senior leaders, was addressing a press conference at BJP headquarter, Trikuta Nagar, Jammu. With regard to questions about NC rebellion post cabinet expansion and speculations linking his visit to efforts of BJP government formation, he refused to make any comment. “Whatever is happening in the National Conference, it is their (NC’s) internal affair. I will not comment on that,” he asserted. “I’m here to address only the issue related to fake propaganda being run by the opposition on Special Intensive Revision (SIR) across the country and particularly in the union capital. For the past few months, the main opposition party Congress and its leader Rahul Gandhi have been busy spreading lies that the Election Commission has manipulated the country's electoral system,” Madhav said. “The Election Commission will reply to these allegations and they have already submitted a detailed affidavit on behalf of all three Election Commissioners in the Supreme Court vis-a-vis entire process of SIR and all facts related to it. But we want to expose Congress’ real intentions behind the controversy they wilfully created to achieve its objective of “regime-change” but not through democratic means. Their leaders are spelling out openly at every public forum and social media that they wanted regime-change like it happened in Bangladesh and Nepal,” he said. It was because the opposition had realised that they could not defeat BJP, the Prime Minister Narenda Modi electorally, so they (Congress and other opposition parties) wanted to overthrow democratically-elected regime and wrest power through anarchy, creating doubts about constitutional institutions, Madhav alleged. “However, the people of India will never allow the Congress to succeed in its intentions to spread anarchy in the country,” he asserted. He described all allegations of Congress regarding SIR exercise, presently underway in many parts of the country and already completed in several states, as “out and out white lies.” BJP national vice president reiterated that the Election Commission, through constitutional exercise SIR, was actually cleansing the electoral system of “all sins of Congress which fiddled with the electoral rolls during the past several decades.” Regarding Congress’ main allegation that the names of 13 crore voters were deleted (through SIR exercise), Madhav questioned why it could not bring those people to the fore. “Where are those 13 Cr voters whose names, according to the Congress, have been deleted? SIR is cleansing electoral rolls of discrepancies through constitutionally valid SIR exercise, happening after a gap of 20 years. The names of dead (around 2-3 Cr), transferred (around 6 Cr), non-existent voters (1 or 2 Cr) and infiltrators who are illegal voters have been deleted and are being deleted. Like in Jammu, Rohingyas have settled at many places. The names of such infiltrators, illegal immigrants get deleted. This is imperative. Referring to the Congress allegations against the Modi government of “committing electoral frauds”, Madhav asserted, “In fact, in the history of the country, two Prime Ministers actually committed such proven electoral frauds. One was Indira Gandhi, whose election was declared “illegal” by Allahabad court proving the charge that the official election machinery was misused by her to emerge victorious. In response, Indira imposed an emergency in the country. Secondly in 1987 in J&K assembly elections, the then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi in league with Farooq Abdullah had resorted to large-scale irregularities in the election process, leading to emergence of terrorism here (in J&K. These are well-recorded facts.”

stories.headline: Lower Costs, Tariffs Make India Data Centre Rentals 30-35% Cheaper: Crisil
stories.title: Lower Costs, Tariffs Make India Data Centre Rentals 30-35% Cheaper: Crisil
stories.summary: India’s data centre industry is entering an investment supercycle, with installed capacity expected to increase five-fold to about 7.5 gigawatts (GW) by March 2030, according to a research report by Crisil Ratings. According to Anand Kulkarni, Director, Crisil Ratings, India's structural cost advantages are strengthening its position as a data centre destination. Development costs are around one-fifth lower than in several competing Asia-Pacific markets, owing to more competitive land, construction and labour costs. He added, "Combined with lower power tariffs , this translates into rentals that are 30-35% lower than in peer markets. The ability to develop large, renewable-powered campuses also aligns well with the sustainability goals of hyperscalers, reinforcing India’s competitive positioning.” The industry is expected to attract investments of more than Rs. 3 lakh crore over the next four fiscals. This expansion is being driven by generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-led computing demand, enterprise digitalisation and rising data consumption. However, the growing dominance of hyperscalers, which underpins demand visibility, also exposes developers to customer concentration and pricing risks. The capacity leased to hyperscalers is expected to account for 75-80% of the industry's total capacity by fiscal 2030, up from 60-65% in fiscal 2026. While pricing has remained broadly stable so far, accelerating capacity additions and greater bargaining power among hyperscalers could put pressure on rentals and weaken project returns. Data Centre Expansion To Hinge On Power Connectivity And Approvals The report highlights that long-tenor contracts with hyperscalers provide data centre developers with strong cash flow visibility and help reduce offtake risks. However, the pace of capacity expansion and developers' credit quality will depend on timely power connectivity, regulatory approvals and disciplined project execution. Crisil Ratings identifies demand visibility as a key strength for an industry undertaking such a capital-intensive expansion. Nearly half of the upcoming capacity is already committed under long-term contracts, limiting speculative development and reducing offtake risks. Upfront agreements with hyperscalers, supported by cloud adoption and compute-intensive GenAI workloads, provide revenue certainty from the outset. This helps de-risk projects, even as the scale and pace of the planned expansion increase execution requirements. However, the unprecedented pace of development is also creating bottlenecks in power infrastructure, making timely grid connectivity and transmission augmentation increasingly critical. Visakhapatnam, Mumbai And Hyderabad To Emerge As Data Centre Investment Hotspots According to Crisil Ratings, about three-fourths of the upcoming capacity of approximately 6 GW is expected to be developed in Visakhapatnam , Mumbai and Hyderabad. By fiscal 2030, data centre capacity in these cities could rise sharply, reaching levels equivalent to around 80%, 60% and 20%, respectively, of their current peak power demand. This underscores the importance of timely grid connectivity and transmission augmentation. Against this backdrop, disciplined growth backed by firm contracts provides an important safeguard for developers. Existing data centre facilities in India are operating at about 90% utilisation, while more than 95% of the capacity currently under construction is already contracted. This is expected to support a faster cash flows ramp-up once the projects are commissioned. Nitin Bansal, Associate Director, Crisil Ratings, said, “The quality of contracted revenues has also strengthened. Contract tenors have lengthened to 15-20 years from 10-12 years earlier, enhancing cash flow visibility. Furthermore, high migration costs and rising replacement capex should support customer retention, although a meaningful contract renewal track record is yet to be established. At the same time, developers will need to ensure that existing facilities remain relevant for next-generation GenAI workloads through timely investments in upgrades to support higher power density and advanced cooling infrastructure.” Credit Profiles To Depend On Execution And Cash Flow Generation From a credit perspective, the sector's profile will be shaped by the interplay between strong contracted cash flows and front-loaded leverage arising from large upfront capital expenditure. Debt levels are expected to remain elevated over the medium term, as investments typically precede cash generation by 24-36 months. Nevertheless, as projects are commissioned and utilisation ramps up, strong cash flows should support a gradual improvement in leverage. Overall, contracted revenues provide an important anchor for credit stability. However, the unprecedented scale of capacity additions brings execution into sharper focus. Timely commissioning, cost control, adequate power availability and the sustainability of GenAI-led demand growth will remain key factors determining how successfully the industry navigates this investment cycle.

stories.headline: Supreme Court defers Tejpal hearing amid Goa's opposition to release
stories.title: Supreme Court defers Tejpal hearing amid Goa's opposition to release
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 3 : The Supreme Court on Tuesday adjourned till November 5 the hearing on pleas filed by former Tehelka Editor-in-Chief Tarun Tejpal challenging his conviction and 10-year rigorous imprisonment sentence in the 2013 rape case, and by the Goa government seeking enhancement of his sentence. A Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale deferred the hearing after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, sought an adjournment. Appearing for Tejpal, senior advocate Kapil Sibal did not oppose the request for more time but urged the apex court to allow his client to come home during Diwali. "If he wants to take time, he can take time. But let (Tejpal) come out during Diwali," Sibal submitted. Opposing the request, SG Mehta submitted that Tejpal stood convicted. However, Sibal countered, saying, "So what? It's a reversal of the acquittal. He can come home for Diwali. Why should he be inside?" The Goa government opposed Sibal's request to allow Tejpal to come out of jail during the festival. The matter will now be taken up for further hearing on November 5. The former Tehelka editor has challenged the Bombay High Court judgment that set aside his acquittal by a sessions court and convicted him of rape and other offences under the Indian Penal Code (IPC), sentencing him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment. The case stems from allegations by a junior colleague that Tejpal sexually assaulted her inside an elevator of a luxury hotel in Goa during an event in November 2013. In May 2021, a sessions court acquitted Tejpal, holding that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt and referring to alleged lapses in the investigation. The Goa government subsequently challenged the acquittal before the Bombay High Court. On August 6, the Bombay High Court set aside the acquittal and convicted Tejpal under Sections 376(2)(f) and 376(2)(k) (rape), 354A (sexual harassment) and 354B (assault or use of criminal force against a woman with intent to disrobe) of the IPC. The Goa government has separately approached the Supreme Court seeking enhancement of the 10-year rigorous imprisonment sentence imposed by the High Court. Tejpal surrendered before the Additional Sessions Court at Mapusa in Goa on September 14, following the Supreme Court's direction rejecting his plea for exemption from surrender. He was subsequently taken to Central Jail in Colvale, North Goa, to serve his sentence. --IANS

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today (November 3) expressed its disappointment that 23 States/Union Territories (UTs) are yet to respond to the information sought by the Union Home Ministry in the suo motu case on caste-based discrimination inside prisons.
It has, therefore, given them one last opportunity to respond.

A bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Manmohan warned that if the States/UTs fail to respond by the next date of hearing (January 13), it would be “compelled to direct the Chief Secretaries/Principal Secretaries of all the States/UTs to personally remain present before this Court.” The observations were made while hearing the matter (In Re: Discrimination Inside Prisons in India) in which Senior Advocate (Dr) S Muralidhar is appointed as the Amicus Curiae.
The case arose from the Supreme Court's judgment in Sukanya Shantha v Union of India and Others, wherein directions were issued to address caste-based discrimination in prisons.
The Court later took up this suo motu cognizance to monitor the compliance.

In July this year, the Court took on record a detailed Status Report which showed the written responses still awaited from several States/UTs on the method of collection and transmission of caste data to the NCRB; deletion of caste columns in all prison registers and forms; outsourcing of cleaning work; compliance with the guidelines in Arnesh Kumar and Amanatullah Khan; notifications constituting Boards of Visitors district-wise; the status of new Acts/Rules/Manuals proposed by States/UTs; and the status of amendments to offending provisions in the Acts/Rules/Manuals.
The Court had asked Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati to take up the matter with all States/UTs and gather the information at the earliest.
Muralidhar also apprised the Court that no State/UT had constituted a Board of Visitors (BoVs) district-wise, as directed in July this year.
It had directed all State Governments/UTs to constitute district-wise BoVs, headed by the Principal District Judge of that particular District, within a period of four weeks from the date of order.
In September this year, the Court noted some progress in constituting the BoVs.
It was informed that only a few districts of different States had constituted them.
Today, the bench took serious note of the non-compliance and warned for personal presence of the officials if the report is not filed by the next date of hearing.

article_sentences: India is focusing on building a robust domestic defence ecosystem as strategic autonomy and indigenous military capabilities are essential to effectively deal with national security challenges, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Tuesday.

In an address at a meeting of the Consultative Committee of the defence ministry in Jaisalmer, Singh said the government has been boosting the domestic defence industry as part of efforts to reduce the country's strategic dependence on foreign sources.
"Strategic autonomy and indigenous technological capabilities are essential to safeguarding national security," he said.

The meeting witnessed comprehensive deliberations on emerging security challenges, warfare paradigms, technological advancements and the imperative of building a future-ready, technologically empowered and operationally agile military.

The key focus areas that emerged during the deliberations included accelerating the induction of next-generation platforms and weapon systems and strengthening the tri-service integration, joint operational planning and synergised application of capabilities.

In his remarks, the defence minister emphasised the need for the military to remain prepared to combat emerging challenges and listed the steps taken by the government across key dimensions such as "budget and capital acquisition" and "technology and human capital" to equip the military to meet the evolving demands of technology-driven modern warfare.

He highlighted the government's sustained focus on budgetary support and capital acquisition to meet the modernisation requirements, stressing that adequate financial resources, coupled with effective utilisation and prioritisation of critical needs of the services.
Singh said the defence budget for financial year 2026-27 was increased to a record Rs 7.85 lakh crore, including a capital outlay of Rs 2.19 lakh crore.
On the vision of self-reliance in defence, he said that defence production has risen from Rs 46,429 crore in 2014-15 to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26.
The defence exports, which stood at less than Rs 2,000 crore in 2014, increased to approximately Rs 40,000 crore.
"We aim to achieve defence production worth Rs 3 lakh crore and defence exports worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029," he added.
Singh underlined the transformative role of technology in modern warfare, stating that technological advancements are integral to the changing character of conflicts.
